newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Lufthansa restores 11th HK-FRA 747 freighter.
newsitem.headline: Lufthansa restores 11th HK-FRA 747 freighter.

text.p: Lufthansa Cargo is to add a 11th weekly freighter flight between Hong Kong and Frankfurt from March 31, the airline's managing director for China, Hong Kong and Taiwan, Christian Sedelmaier, has told Reuters.
The German flag carrier currently operates five weekly Boeing 747-200 Freighters in a joint venture with Cathay Pacific Cargo which operates the remaining five.

The 11th frequency on Mondays starting on Easter Monday will be a Lufthansa Boeing 747-200 via the airline's cargo hub in the Gulf, Sharjah. The additional 100 tonnes capacity will be split equally between Lufthansa and Cathay, Sedelmaier said.

Last October, Lufthansa Cargo increased capacity from 10 to 11 freighters a week because of high demand but the extra frequency was withdrawn after the Christmas peak, Frank Berweger, Lufthansa Cargo's general manager for Hong Kong, Macau and southern China said in a Reuters interview.

"We are doing something which we have never done before and increasing capacity in what is expected to be a slack season when the market normally drops. But we have confidence in the market and hope we can fill that capacity," Berweger added.

According to Civil Aviation Department statistics, the Hong Kong-Frankfurt route, which is exclusively flown by Cathay and Lufthansa, is the most important single non-Asian trade route for Hong Kong's imports and exports.
Latest figures for December 1996 show both carriers exported 4,572 tonnes of air cargo from Hong Kong with 4,457 of imports being flown from Germany. --Reuters Air Cargo Newsroom
